chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about salat (prayer) by night and day when the sun, the moon, and the stars cannot be seen. He said: “Exert your judgment and deliberately face the qiblah to the best of your ability.”

key_terms.اجْتَهِدْ: exert yourself in reasoning and effort
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: night, one of the times mentioned for performing salat (prayer)
key_terms.النَّهَارِ: daytime, the other time mentioned for performing salat (prayer)
key_terms.جُهْدَكَ: to the extent of your ability and utmost effort

ai.seo_question: What should a person do to determine the qiblah for salat (prayer) when the sun, moon, and stars are not visible?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for performing salat (prayer) when natural signs used for orientation are not visible. It instructs the believer to use personal judgment and strive to face the qiblah as best as possible, showing that obligation is tied to one’s capacity.
